note: How a feature loop's run is read from in-the-loop: the run records under llm-dlc/traces/{session}/runs/, joined to that session's prompts by time. Prompt text is read only to tell who sent a prompt, and is never published.
window: A prompt, a tool call or a commit belongs to a run when it starts in [the record's Started time, its Ended or Stopped time]. A run with no end recorded lasts until its session's next run starts, or until its last prompt from the loop ends.

senders.note: Who sent a prompt that the trace records as typed input, by the start of its text. The first matching group wins; a prompt that matches none was typed by a person. Before these, a prompt that opens with the instruction a run record quotes under its header is the harness's: the opening words up to a list's place ({}), at most 80 characters and at least 16, as the source's loop_stats.py reads them.
harness: ^Cycle \d+ of the feature loop is committed
^This conversation goes on as one of the parallel streams
^You decided that the loop stops after
^Add more advanced features along with examples to the jvmcontract
^Add more advanced examples showcasing verification of TLA
^Enhance the jvmcontract library to be more useful to expert
senders.harnessNote: The last four are the fixed prompts feature-loop.sh sent before it worked from briefs (Oct 31 to Nov 4, 2026). Each was checked against the script's own history.

drivers: Who set off a tool call: the sender of the latest prompt before it in its session. A prompt from the loop's script is 'loop'; one a person typed, or their interrupt, is 'person'; a notification that background work finished keeps the driver it follows; a slash command, a message from another agent, and anything before a session's first prompt are 'other', because the trace doesn't say who sent them.

scripts.note: The loop's own scripts. Their commits are listed as the loop's history, read from a git checkout.

campaign: A loop belongs to the campaign of the shortest brief name that equals its own or that it extends with '-': foundations-heap runs in the campaign foundations when a brief named foundations exists. Brief names are the files of llm-dlc/loops/ at the source revision, and the names of the runs themselves.

outcomes.note: How a run ended, from its record's Ended or Stopped line. The first matching pattern wins; no such line is 'open': the record doesn't say the run ended.

patterns.pattern: still says working|needs attention|made no commit|brief changed|gave no clear
decided the work was done|the brief says done
